description: Opt-in overlay for repositories whose CI is the gate: minor, patch, digest and pin updates skip the dashboard tick, share one branch and merge themselves once the pull request checks are green, after a release-age soak. Majors and Go toolchain minors keep the tick. Extend after the default preset and after golang when the repository has one.

packageRules.description: Minor, patch and pin updates share one branch and open without a dashboard tick. One pull request per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a CI run each time it is rebased.
Without the tick the soak returns, so a freshly published release is not proposed the hour it appears.

Non-major updates share one branch and merge themselves once its checks are green. One grouped branch per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a full CI run each time it is rebased, and a small runner pool cannot absorb twenty of them per push. An automerging branch rebases when it falls behind: with rebaseWhen conflicted it would keep a red result from an old base forever, and one branch rebased once per Renovate run costs at most one CI run an hour. internalChecksFilter strict keeps an unsoaked update out of the group instead of holding the whole branch.
With minor and patch combined, Renovate offers only the highest non-major Go version, a minor that waits for approval, so the toolchain patch would never be proposed. Go keeps them apart.

A Go toolchain minor decides what compiles the shipped binaries and raises the floor for contributors. It stays a deliberate, dashboard-approved change outside the group; toolchain patches still merge themselves.
Go toolchain patches merge themselves in their own branch: kept apart from minors, they cannot share the non-major group's branch.

Shared preset bumps merge themselves once the pull request checks are green: no dashboard tick, no release-age soak, their own branch. The preset is Webgrip's own reviewed code, released from this repository, and every consumer waiting for a tick on it is a policy fix that has not landed. Renovate's automerge, not the platform's, so a branch without checks does not merge at once. It is never digest-pinned: It is already pinned to a protected semver release tag; the global pinDigests=true otherwise makes Renovate try to rewrite 'github>webgrip/renovate-config#vX.Y.Z' to a commit SHA, the replacement never applies ('Digest is not updated'), and the whole pin-dependencies branch aborts with 'Error updating branch: update failure' on every run. A preset bump changes how Renovate treats the repository, not what it ships, so it lands as chore(renovate) and never cuts a release.. The generator appends this part to every preset it builds, so no grouping, soak or commit-type rule of an earlier part can catch the bump.
